Solution 3 is wrong. Its counting argument assumes that every star contributes 3−p_i edges to the answer-1 branch, which holds only when the star's centre is in T. For a star with its centre outside T, the answer-1 branch gets p_i edges instead. Redoing the count with x centre-in stars gives a consistent first test. Taking 9 centre-in stars with p_i=3 gives branches (3⁹), (2⁹,1⁹), and (2⁹,1⁹). Each has sum 27 and is ⪯_w N(3)=(8,7,4,4,1,1,1,1), and k=3 sufficiency is accepted by all three solutions, so M(3²⁷) ≤ 4. Solution 3 therefore has no valid counterexample at k=4 and cannot be right.

Solutions 1 and 2 disagree on whether a counterexample exists. I could not verify either side's computations here. Solution 1 gives an explicit list at k=6 that is ⪯_w N(6): replacing the block (22,7¹⁶) with (8¹⁵,7²) keeps the same total and gives prefix sums that are no larger. Its claim that no counterexample exists at k=5 rests on a search it admits is not exhaustive. Solution 2 reports no counterexample anywhere but gives no explicit list. A verifiable k=6 counterexample is more informative than an absence claim, so Solution 1 is the more plausible of the two, though its answer of 6 depends on the unverified k=5 claim.

CHOICE: 1
